tools.name: search_slots
tools.description: Search bookable sports slots in London across every provider LayUp aggregates. Use when a user wants to find a court, pitch, lane, class or pickup game for football, tennis, squash, padel or swimming. Filter by sport, area/borough, date range, time of day and max price. tools.name: refine_search
tools.description: Find out WHERE and WHEN there is availability, before asking the user a clarifying question. Takes the same filters as search_slots and returns counts by area, day, time band and price — not slots. tools.name: list_sports
tools.description: List the sports LayUp covers with a count of slots available in the next 7 days. Useful as a quick overview before a more specific search.

tools.name: get_venue
tools.description: List upcoming bookable slots at a single venue, identified by its venue_slug (as returned by search_slots). Use to drill into one venue after a search.

tools.name: create_alert
tools.description: Set up an email alert for the user: LayUp watches for NEW matching slots (e.g. a cancellation freeing up a peak court) and emails them when one appears. Use when the user can't find a slot now and wants to be notified, or asks to 'monitor'/'watch'/'let me know when'. Requires their email. NARROW IT

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.layupsport.com" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_alert · Public sink: create_alert.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_alert · Public sink: create_alert

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "create_alert" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
